items.description: Median tonnage and grade of deposit types, with the log10 spread of each (USGS grade-tonnage models)
items.unit: tonnage Mt; grade unit in the row label; spreads in log10 units
items.note: Read from the bulletin's grade and tonnage figures on 2026-10-14 (models 17, 20c, 36a, 25c, 28a, 31a, 15c, 18d, 18b, 14a, 34a, 39a and 34c, the upwelling type). Each spread is (log10 p10 - log10 p90) / 2.563 from the figure's 90th and 10th percentile arrows. Kuroko zinc (median 2.0% Zn) reaches no 90th percentile, so it has no spread and no row. This replaced an earlier transcription made without the bulletin, which had Fe skarn at 49% Fe, phosphorite at 200 Mt and 24% P2O5, and placer gold at 0.25 g/t.

items.description: Diamond grade of mined kimberlite pipes
items.note: Descriptive model 12 (printed p. 54): mined kimberlites yield 0.1 to 0.6 ppm diamond, which is 0.5 to 3 ct/t at 0.2 g per carat. The bulletin gives no grade-tonnage model for diamond pipes, and most pipes are never mined.

Typical upper-crustal geothermal gradient on continents
items.note: Mean continental heat flow 65 mW/m2 (Pollack et al. 1993) with conductivity ~2.5 W/(m K).

items.description: Tonnage and gold grade of alluvial placer gold deposits (65 deposits, predominantly Quaternary) at the 90th, 50th and 10th percentiles
items.note: Read from the bulletin's figs. 196 and 197 on 2026-10-14. The authors converted volumes to tonnes at 2.0 t/m3 (item placer_gravel_density). Gold grade correlates with tonnage (r = -0.35). The descriptive model sites placers where gradients flatten and river velocities lessen.

items.description: Volume and diamond grade of diamond placers (25 deposits, mostly alluvial, some residual over kimberlite pipes, beach placers excluded) at the 90th, 50th and 10th percentiles
items.unit: volume million m3; grade carats per m3
items.note: Read from figs. 48 (size) and 49 (grade) on 2026-10-23. Workings within 1.5 km count as one deposit. The model gives volume, not tonnes; the island converts it at model 39a's 2.0 t/m3 for wet sand and gravel (placer_gravel_density), a stand-in (D56).

items.description: Tonnage and platinum grade of placer PGE-Au deposits (83 deposits, all in the Urals) at the 90th, 50th and 10th percentiles
items.unit: tonnage million tonnes; platinum parts per billion
items.note: Read from figs. 198 (tonnage) and 199A (platinum) on 2026-10-23. Gold is reported in only about a tenth of the deposits (fig. 199B, 10th percentile 0.048 g/t), so the island gives these sites platinum only. The authors note the platinum plot suggests three populations, dredged and conventional placers mixed.

items.description: Recovered or reported grade of alluvial diamond gravels, carats per 100 tonnes (cpht); columns are the low and high ends of each reported range (equal where a single figure)
items.note: almas_lanyon: 'Recoverable diamond grades are generally low (0.30 to 0.80 cpht)'; 'Historic bulk sampling on the Wouterspan B terrace deliver grades between 0.4 – 0.6 cpht' ... 'totalling 820ct at an average grade of 0.53 cpht' (Lanyon Vale project page). ggsm_2012 (rows 3 and 4, source differs from the item source): 'The results show an average yield of 56 carats per hundred tonne (Cpht) of hi-grade diamonds, slightly above the average grade of Sierra Leone, which, according to the comprehensive report undertaken in the 1970s by PK Hall, shows an average of approximately 50 Cpht.' Promoter release, preliminary, 2012. Two orders of magnitude between Orange River terraces and Sierra Leone gravels. Namibian marine/beach grades per tonne were not found.

items.description: Solar sea-salt harvest per hectare of total saltworks footprint, Lake Grassmere NZ, in a normal year (arithmetic: 60,000-70,000 t / 1416 ha)
items.unit: t salt per ha of total solar salt production area per year
items.note: Derived by me. Dominion Salt 'Our Locations': 'Some 60,000 – 70,000 tonnes of salt are harvested from Lake Grassmere each year.' Fact sheet p. 2: 'The total area for solar salt production at Lake Grassmere is approximately 1416 hectares' (688 ha main lake, 486 ha concentrating, 81 ha final, 20 ha deep storage, 93 ha crystallising, 40 ha re-concentrating, 8 ha wash brine). 60,000/1416 = 42.4; 70,000/1416 = 49.4. Per hectare of crystalliser only (93 ha) would be roughly 15 times higher. No FAO or other temperate source found.

items.description: Lake Grassmere annual harvest extremes, and equivalent per-hectare yield over 1416 ha
items.note: Fact sheet p. 3: 'annual harvests have ranged from a nil harvest in 1986 to a maximum yield of 130,000 in 1998.' Also: 'Salt production is highly dependent on the amount of rainfall'; 'The salt crust thickness may vary from 25mm to 75mm when harvested, depending on evaporation and particularly the rainfall'; 'The yearly average rainfall is 610mm'. Unit of 130,000 assumed tonnes (sheet omits unit). 130,000/1416 = 91.8 is my arithmetic.

items.description: Alluvial bulk-sample diamond grade, Lulo (Lunda Norte, Angola), per 100 cubic metres of in-situ gravel
items.note: p. 1: 'The completed BLK_29 alluvial bulk sample (Table 1) produced diamond grades of 35.02 carats per 100 cubic metres. The average size of the diamonds recovered from BLK_29 was 1.81 carats.' Table notes: 'Grade is quoted in carats per 100 cubic metres of in-situ gravel.' Volume basis, single block, bottom screen 1.2 mm; not convertible to per-tonne without a gravel bulk density.
